doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Surprise re-use payments
summary: Hey gets small re-use checks for 9 to 5, I Love L.A. and Donna Summer records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Do you get envelopes in the mail on occasion with payments for things that you didn’t expect?

Yeah. Not a lot, but every once in a while. Dolly Parton’s “9 to 5” is like $110 every couple of years I guess sort of. I played on “I Love L.A.” with Randy Newman on the session that we did on that record. The bridge part of it, if you know that [scats] I said, they said, “Well what do you think about on this song?” And I said, “What about like a mariachi kind of thing, you know ‘I Love L.A.’ a mariachi.” So I played that mariachi style, it kind of sounded like Herb Alpert in harmony parts you know. If they used it, it’s really soft in the mix. But because I’m on the contract for that, when they use “I Love L.A.” I get a re-use for that. What else? Oh I just got a Donna Summer re-use for, you know we did all those disco records that she did so I just got — and that was $80 or
something you know, like that. You know not a lot, but every once in a while something comes in.
